subject: general
question: The Principal of a Sanskrit College who represented a blend of Indian and Western culture was __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Principal of a Sanskrit College** who represented a blend of **Indian and Western culture** was** Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**.
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was born to Thakurdas Bandyopadhyay and Bhagavati Devi.
 
• From a young age, he displayed remarkable intelligence and a strong passion for learning.
 
• He pursued his education at the Sanskrit College in Calcutta and successfully passed the law examination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy **was an Indian reformer and a founding member of the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later evolved into the Brahmo Samaj, a significant social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen** was a Hindu philosopher and social reformer who endeavored to blend Christian theology with Hindu philosophy.
 
• Debendranath Tagore, an Indian philosopher and religious reformer, played an active role in the Brahmo Samaj and became a member in 1842.
